"Exceptional dining experience from start to finish! The food was absolutely outstanding—every dish was freshly prepared, full of rich flavors, and presented beautifully. You can truly taste the quality of the ingredients in every bite.
The service was top-tier, the staff were welcoming and attentive, and the overall ambiance made the meal even more enjoyable. Hands down one of the best food experiences I’ve had in a long time. Highly recommend to anyone looking for great food and great vibes!"
At Anna Nagar

​A fantastic meal across the board with top-notch flavors.

​Had an extensive meal here and was thoroughly impressed with the quality and consistency coming out of the kitchen. Almost every dish hit the mark.

​Caribbean Calypso: Absolute standout of the meal. The meatballs were finely minced, perfectly seasoned with herbs and spices, fried just right, and paired with a finger-licking good sauce.

​Chicken Pesto Pasta: Beautifully prepared. The pesto was fragrant and rich, the cheese added great creaminess, and the accompanying garlic bread was delightfully crisp.

​Chilli Garlic Chicken Fried Rice: Generous portion with a strong, aromatic garlic punch. The chicken pieces were tender and cooked spot-on.

​Wok-Tossed Beef: Very rich flavor profile and cooked to ideal tenderness. Noticeable hint of fish sauce/flavor in the toss, but it didn’t detract from the dish at all.

​Strawberry Cloud Cake: Soft, spongy, and bursting with rich flavor. High quality and a genuinely delicious dessert.

​Lotus Biscoff Shake: Solid shake with an intense Biscoff flavor, though strictly for serious sweet tooths as it leans very sweet.

​Overall, a great dining experience with memorable dishes. Definitely worth a visit!

Urban Spatula has a relaxed, distinctive setup, with a café downstairs and the restaurant upstairs. I appreciated how approachable the service team was and how willing they were to offer useful recommendations without being pushy. It felt like an easy place to settle into, whether stopping by the café or heading up for a meal. I’d happily return.

I recently visited this hotel with high expectations, especially because the ambiance is actually quite good. The place looks well-designed, clean, and has a pleasant atmosphere that makes you feel like you’re in for a nice dining experience. Unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

The food quality was extremely disappointing and honestly unacceptable. We ordered malai tandoori chicken, and to our shock, it was served raw and undercooked. This is not just a small mistake — serving uncooked chicken is a serious health risk and completely irresponsible from a restaurant of this standard. It clearly shows a lack of basic quality control and kitchen discipline.

Hoping it was just a one-time issue, we also tried the chicken Manchurian, but that turned out to be equally bad. The gravy tasted overwhelmingly like bottled tomato sauce, almost like a whole bottle of Kissan tomato sauce was poured into it. There was no balance of flavours, no authentic taste — just a sweet, artificial, and very unpleasant experience.

It’s very disappointing when a place that invests so much in ambiance completely fails in the most important aspect — food quality and safety. Serving uncooked chicken is not something that can be ignored or justified. It raises serious concerns about hygiene standards and overall kitchen practices.

Overall, while the ambiance might attract you initially, the food is a complete letdown. I would strongly advise others to be cautious before dining here, especially when it comes to non-vegetarian dishes. A restaurant can improve taste over time, but food safety is something that should never be compromised.

Urban Spatula is one of those Anna Nagar comfort spots where the ambience does half the talking. Warm lights, wooden interiors and a menu that jumps from kebabs to pasta without hesitation. Not chasing fine-dining tags, but a dependable place for family dinners, casual meetups and office gatherings when everyone wants something different on the table.

Urban Club Sandwich – 9/10 Comes with fries and ketchup on the side. Packed with chicken, egg, cheese, cucumber and tomatoes. The layers hold together well without feeling heavy. Easily one of the best sandwiches I’ve had in Chennai.

Char Kway Teow Chicken Noodles – 7/10 | ₹450 Originally wanted to try their Pad Thai Noodles, but that’s temporarily off the menu. Settled for the Char Kway Teow Chicken Noodles instead. A spicy sauce coats the noodles, while crunchy broccoli and cabbage add texture. Decent portion size and flavour, though it didn’t quite match the high set by the sandwich.

TasteRx says: Go for the Club Sandwich alone and you won’t be disappointed. The noodles are a decent supporting act, but the sandwich is the reason I’d return.

google_reviews.body: Time Cafe, Chennai, is a cozy and relaxing place to spend quality time with friends and family. The ambiance is pleasant, the food is tasty, and the staff is friendly and attentive. A great spot for casual hangouts, coffee dates, and enjoying some peaceful moments. Highly recommended!✨🧋

Time Cafe in Nungambakkam turned out to be a lovely little discovery for us. It is a cosy, zen spot tucked away from the hustle & bustle of the city & the constant honking.

It has a relaxed cafe-and-boutique feel, the kind of place where you can sit comfortably, chat, sip coffee, and enjoy food that is thoughtfully prepared.

We tried the chicken sheekh kebabs, fish fingers, ginger-spiced tea, cold Spanish lattes, pasta Alfredo & their chocolate cake which was truly to die for.

What made the experience even better was speaking to the owner, who came across as a very humble and sincere gentleman. He explained that they do not use white sugar or maida in their preparations, and even source for country chicken. The pasta Alfredo too was made with wheat, which was a pleasant surprise.

The food had a very clean, wholesome taste without compromising on flavour. Everything felt thoughtfully prepared , tasty, comforting, & guilt-free in the best way.

One thing to note is that the vegetarian options are quite limited, so expanding the veg menu would make the place even better. That said, the staff were courteous, polite, and very responsive whenever we asked for clarifications or assistance, which is always appreciated.
They also offer valet parking, which is a big plus given the Nungambakkam location. Overall, it’s a good café with a pleasant vibe, friendly service, and a great place to unwind and spend quality time. Would definitely consider visiting again.

Fristo – Phenomenal Loaded Fries, But the "Cheese Blast" Falls Short

​If you are looking for a quick, no-frills spot for some heavy, flavor-packed street food, Fristo is worth a stop. Just keep in mind that this isn't a sit-down restaurant—there is no dining space, so you’ll just have to stand, grab your food, and enjoy it on the spot.

​Here is how the food fared during our visit:
​The Absolute Winner: Chicken Loaded Fries
​If you visit Fristo, you cannot skip the Chicken Loaded Fries. This dish was the undisputed star of the show.

​The Blend: It’s a perfect combination of well-cooked chicken, crispy french fries, and melty cheese.

​The X-Factor: What elevates this dish is their secret sauce. When all three main ingredients combine with that sauce, every bite is incredibly flavorful and satisfying. Highly recommended!

​The Mixed Bag: Cheese Blast Burgers (Beef vs. Chicken)
​We ordered two variations of their signature Cheese Blast Burger, and the experience was night and day when it came to texture, though both tasted good flavor-wise.

​The Beef Burger (Soft & Right): This one was spot on. Both the burger bun and the beef patty were beautifully soft, making it easy and enjoyable to eat.

​The Chicken Burger (Too Hard): Unfortunately, this one missed the mark on texture. Both the bun and the chicken patty were quite hard, which took away from the overall enjoyment.

​The Big Letdown: For a burger explicitly named the "Cheese Blast," the cheese element was a major disappointment. There was only a tiny amount of cheese inside. It definitely didn't live up to the name or the hype of a "blast."

​The Verdict
​Fristo is a great street-style spot for a quick bite, provided you know what to order. Skip the chicken burger, go for the beef if you want a soft, flavorful burger, and absolutely do not leave without ordering the Chicken Loaded Fries—they completely stole the spotlight.

​The Highlights
​Chennai-Style Biriyani: This was the star of the show. If you are coming here for the Biriyani, you won't be disappointed. It was flavorful and well-cooked.

​Service & Logistics
​Wait Time: Expect a rush. Even with a 15–20 minute wait, the place stays packed.
​Value: At ₹1,600, it feels like a mixed bag. You're paying a premium for a meal where only half the dishes truly shine.
​Final Verdict: Go for the Biriyani and the Kunafa. Skip the rest of the starters and sides, as they don't match the quality of the main dish.

google_reviews.body: The flavors here reminded me of Malaysian food, with a noticeable extra richness that suits India’s spice culture. I tried the teh tarik, nasi lemak with chicken, and nasi kandar, and the meal was enjoyable overall. As a Malaysian, I came here genuinely craving some Roti Canai and Nasi Lemak and thought, why not stop by for a quick makan? Unfortunately, for the prices being charged, what was served was nowhere near the standard I expected from a place carrying the Nasi Kandar Pelita name.

The Nasi Lemak especially was disappointing. Presentation aside, the dish simply had no soul. Everything tasted unnecessarily sweet, to the point where the flavours didn’t make sense together. Even the rice lacked that proper coconut milk fragrance and richness that is literally the foundation of a good Nasi Lemak.

What made the experience worse was the response when I questioned whether this was genuinely how they intended their Nasi Lemak to taste. Instead of taking the feedback constructively, I was met with faces and the “this is a Malaysian-style restaurant” card.

Bruh, I’m Malaysian myself. 😭 Please don’t teach a Malaysian what Nasi Lemak is supposed to taste like.

If you’re going to represent and sell the food of my country, then at least do justice to it. I’m not expecting every plate in Chennai to taste exactly like KL or Penang, but the fundamentals should still be there, especially when you are branding yourself as a Malaysian speciality restaurant.

Nasi Kandar Pelita, please seriously keep an eye on this outlet and its preparation standards. Having Malaysian-themed uniforms, décor and branding does not automatically make the food authentically Malaysian. Without the taste and quality to back it up, those things just become gimmicks.

₹400 for a plate of Nasi Lemak Ayam is not exactly cheap either. At that price, customers deserve something prepared with considerably more care and authenticity.

I really wanted to like this place because seeing Malaysian food represented in Chennai genuinely got me excited. Sadly, I walked away feeling that the Malaysian identity was stronger in the branding than it was on the plate. 🇲🇾

It's easily accessible and provides a sanctuary amidst the bustling mall environment. The management has thoughtfully provided separate ablution facilities, ensuring cleanliness and convenience for worshippers.
Moreover, the khutbahs (sermons) delivered during Jummah prayers are thought-provoking and spiritually uplifting. The imam is knowledgeable and engages the audience with relevant and timely topics, making the Friday prayers even more meaningful.
In conclusion, if you're in search of a small but remarkable Jummah prayer hall, I highly recommend visiting the one in Forum Mall. I have truly found solace and fulfillment in my Friday prayers at this wonderful establishment.
